text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- President Hosni Mubarak said stability in the Middle East was important for the whole region, including Israel. he added: "We don't want wars in the region. We want there to be development and stability. The whole world is not looking for wars, because where there is war, there is chaos and development comes to an end." He also said that U.S. Presifdent Bill Clinton was the key to the peace process.
- Clinton says the differences remain and negotiations will start at the Erez crossing on Sunday.

- Mubarak, in interview with the armed forces magazine Defence, said that for the peace process to succeed U.S. policy must fill in the gaps. This policy was able to put an end to the Serb massacres in Bosnia and by the same standards it must put an end to differences obstructing Middle East peace.

- In an interview with al-Ahram Weekly, presidential adviser Osama el-Baz said Israel had wanted to hold the Middle Easdt summit in Cairo but it backed out when Egypt submitted specific demands for ensuring the summit succeeded. He said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lacked experience and was following a policy marked by intellectual rigidity.
- Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan arrives in Cairo, says that the Israeli-Turkish military cooperation agreement covers only aircraft maintenance.

- Ali Hassan of the Supreme Council for Antiquities said the council's mission to Pharaoh's island in the Gulf of Aqaba had found military installations and reinforcements which show they were built in the time of Saladin, starting from AD 1170.
AL-AKHBAR
- President Mubarak has massive public reception on his trip to Aswan, the New Valley and Luxor.
- Mubarak received a phone call from President Clinton to brief him on the Washington summit. He also had a phone call from King Hussein of Jordan, also on the summit.
- A man tried to export 2,000 scorpions and 150 cobras for sale to collectors. He was taking them by boat from the Red Sea port of Safaga.
- Talks between Erbakan and Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri start today.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Washington summit fails, because of Netanyahu.
- Mubarak said: "We don't take any decision without study, our aim is to have peace and develop the region."
- Erbakan said provocative actions by Israel would lead only to tension in the Middle East and would not bring about peace.
AL-WAFD
- Washington summit fails. Israel says it won and achieved all its demands. Clinton refuses to put pressure on Netanyahu and says no agreement reached on the tunnel.
